# Baseera evaluation (generated by `make eval`, do not edit by hand)

- Test set: `data/testset/labeled.csv` — 105 URLs (43 fraudulent, 62 benign).
- **The fraudulent examples are SYNTHETIC** (invented look-alikes written by the team). Benign examples are real public sites, except 9 rows whose note says invented/illustrative (benign URL shapes such as a shared-platform sub-domain or an illustrative path on an official domain). These numbers show the engine behaves as designed; they are NOT a measurement of real-world accuracy.
- Mode: offline (no RDAP/TLS/redirect lookups, synthetic blocklist disabled).
- Decision rule: fraudulent if risk >= 30 (the 'medium' threshold in data/weights.yaml).

## Confusion matrix at the current threshold

| | predicted fraud | predicted benign |
|---|---|---|
| actual fraud | TP 41 | FN 2 |
| actual benign | FP 1 | TN 61 |

Precision **0.98**, Recall **0.95**, F1 **0.96**, FPR **0.02**

Latency per URL (offline): median 0.95 ms, p95 1.35 ms
